exposure: previous cesarean section or any uterine surgery
cohort: Pregnant women of reproductive age from a rural field practice area in Odisha, India.
finding: The study found a 25.17% prevalence of high-risk pregnancies in rural areas, with previous cesarean section being the most common risk factor, and observed a 96.50% enrollment rate in the Mamata conditional cash transfer scheme among eligible participants.
mod_finding: Previous cesarean section was identified as the most common high-risk factor, accounting for 38.88% of identified high-risk pregnancies.
